subtitle: Mission Control in one click
promotional_text: Name your Spaces and see the names in Mission Control. Built for remote sessions and PC keyboards: Mission Control, App Exposé and Spaces, one click away.
keywords: mission control,spaces,desktop names,expose,show desktop,menu bar,remote desktop,screen sharing,vnc
description:
Mission Control Launcher puts the macOS desktop overview one click away, in the menu bar.

Mission Control, App Exposé and Show Desktop are normally reached with a trackpad swipe, a dedicated key or a hot corner. A lot of setups have none of those, and for those users this app is the difference between having Mission Control and not having it at all:

• Remote users. Screen Sharing, Apple Remote Desktop, VNC and RDP clients keep the gestures and most function keys for themselves. A three-finger swipe never reaches the Mac, F3 does something on the local machine instead, and hot corners are not forwarded. Shortcuts are a guess: from a PC the keys map differently, and even Mac to Mac the remote software can't always tell whether ⌃↑ or ⌘Space is meant for your Mac or the one you're controlling, so the wrong computer's Mission Control or search opens. A click on the menu bar button always lands on the Mac you're controlling.

• PC keyboards. No Mission Control key, no Launchpad key, function keys that map differently, and often no trackpad at all.

• Mice without gestures, KVM switches, docked laptops with the lid closed, and anyone who simply prefers to click.

The menu bar button works in every one of those situations, because a click is all it takes.

WHAT'S IN THE PANEL

• Space names: name the Space you're on, and its name fills its thumbnail in Mission Control, so you can tell Client Work from Email at a glance instead of guessing between Desktop 3 and Desktop 7.

• Quick actions: Mission Control, Apps (Launchpad on older macOS), App Exposé, Show Desktop, previous and next Space, Spotlight, and the Screenshot toolbar.

• Running apps: every open app with its icon. Click one to bring it forward, or quit it.

• Filter: type a few letters to find an app when many are open.

• Global shortcut: ⌃⌥M opens the panel from any app. It can be turned off.

• Open at Login, so the button is always there.

PERMISSIONS, IN PLAIN WORDS

Mission Control, Apps and Screenshot need nothing. App Exposé, Show Desktop, Spaces, Spotlight and quitting apps work by sending the system's own keyboard shortcuts, which macOS only allows once you grant Accessibility access. The app asks the first time you use one of those actions, shows the status in Settings, and never needs anything else.

Space names work on the main display. macOS gives Spaces no lasting ID, so after a restart you name them again, picking from the names you used before.

Mission Control Launcher is sandboxed, has no network access, and collects no data.
review_notes:
Mission Control Launcher is a menu bar utility: no Dock icon and no main window. After launch, click the icon at the right end of the menu bar to open the panel. Right-click it for Settings and Quit.

WHY IT EXISTS
Over Screen Sharing, VNC or RDP, and on PC keyboards, the trackpad swipe, the Mission Control key and hot corners never reach the Mac. The panel replaces all of them with clicks, adds app switching, and names Spaces so a remote user can tell desktops apart.

WHAT TO TRY (no permissions needed)
- Space names: click the icon; the panel's THIS SPACE row says Not named. Click Name..., type a name (e.g. Client Work) and Save: the name shows full screen for a moment. Then click the Mission Control quick action: that Space's thumbnail in the Spaces bar is filled with its name. Add a second Space in Mission Control, switch to it, name it too, and open Mission Control again to see both. Settings has a switch to turn Space names off.
- Quick actions: Mission Control, Apps, Screenshot.
- Running Apps: click an app to switch to it; type in the filter field to narrow the list; the count on the right updates as apps launch and quit.
- Settings via the gear or right-click: Open at Login, the ⌃⌥M global shortcut toggle, and the Accessibility status.
- Press ⌃⌥M from any app to open the panel.

ACTIONS THAT NEED ACCESSIBILITY ACCESS
App Exposé, Show Desktop, Previous/Next Space, Spotlight and quitting an app (hover a row, click the X). The first click shows the standard macOS prompt and opens the app's Settings window, which shows the permission status. Grant it in System Settings > Privacy & Security > Accessibility, then click the action again. These actions send the system's own keyboard shortcuts (⌃↓, F11, ⌃←/⌃→, ⌘Space, ⌘Q), because the App Sandbox allows no other route.

Space names use only public AppKit and Quartz window APIs: one invisible window per Space identifies it, and the name card is an ordinary click-through window shown while Mission Control is open.

The app is sandboxed, has no network entitlement and collects nothing. No account or sign-in.
